lessons.title: Advanced DevTools: Conditional Breakpoints & Logpoints
lessons.description: Go beyond basic breakpoints — use conditional breakpoints to pause only when specific conditions are met.

sections.heading: Conditional breakpoints
paragraphs: Instead of pausing on every execution, conditional breakpoints pause only when a condition is true. This saves enormous time when debugging loops or frequent function calls.
list: Right-click a line number → "Add conditional breakpoint"
Enter a JavaScript expression — pause only when it's truthy
Logpoints: right-click → "Add logpoint" — logs a message without pausing
Both work in Chrome, Firefox and Edge DevTools

codeExamples.heading: Using conditional breakpoints
explanation: Conditional breakpoints avoid pausing on every iteration.
The condition expression is evaluated each time the line is reached.
Logpoints are like console.log without modifying your code.
Both dramatically speed up debugging in loops and frequent functions.

practice.task: Open a JavaScript file in DevTools and set a conditional breakpoint that only pauses when a variable exceeds a certain value.
hints: Right-click the line number in the Sources panel.

keyTakeaways: Conditional breakpoints pause only when a specific condition is met.
Logpoints log messages to the console without pausing execution.
Both are available in Chrome, Firefox and Edge DevTools.
Use them to debug loops, frequent functions and specific data values.
lessons.challenge: Use a conditional breakpoint to find the first item in an array where price exceeds $100 in a loop of 1000 items.

lessons.title: DOM Mutation & Event Listener Breakpoints
lessons.description: Pause execution when the DOM changes or when specific events fire — without setting manual breakpoints.

sections.heading: DOM mutation breakpoints
paragraphs: DevTools can pause when specific DOM changes occur. This is invaluable for debugging dynamic UI updates where you don't know which code is making the change.
list: Pauses on the exact line that modifies the DOM
Event listener breakpoints: pause when specific events fire
Both work in Chrome, Firefox and Edge DevTools

codeExamples.heading: DOM mutation debugging
explanation: DOM mutation breakpoints catch unexpected DOM changes.
You don't need to know which code is responsible — the debugger finds it.
Event listener breakpoints pause when any element receives the specified event.
These are the fastest ways to debug mysterious UI behavior.

practice.task: Use DevTools to set a subtree mutation breakpoint on a <div>. Then write JavaScript that modifies it and verify the debugger pauses.
hints: Right-click the div in Elements panel → Break on → subtree modifications.
The debugger should pause on the line that makes the change.

keyTakeaways: DOM mutation breakpoints pause when an element's subtree, attributes or presence changes.
Event listener breakpoints pause when a specific event fires on any element.
Both are invaluable for debugging dynamic UI behavior.
Use them when you don't know which code is making a change.
lessons.challenge: Debug a scenario where an element disappears unexpectedly using DOM removal breakpoints.

lessons.title: Inspecting Call Stacks & Watching Scope Variables
lessons.description: Use the debugger's Call Stack and Scope panels to understand exactly what's happening at any breakpoint.

sections.heading: The debugger panels
list: Call Stack — shows the chain of function calls that led to the current line
Scope — shows all variables accessible at this point (local, closure, global)
Watch — add expressions to monitor their values as you step through code
Breakpoints — list all your breakpoints with enable/disable toggles

codeExamples.heading: Using Call Stack and Watch
explanation: The Call Stack shows the full execution path — how you got here.
Scope shows all accessible variables — local, closure and global.
Watch lets you add custom expressions to monitor.
Use step buttons (over, into, out) to navigate the stack.

practice.task: Set a debugger statement inside a nested function. When the debugger pauses, examine the Call Stack and identify all enclosing scopes.
hints: Write a function that calls another function that calls a third.
In DevTools, examine the Call Stack panel.

keyTakeaways: The Call Stack shows the chain of function calls that led to the current line.
The Scope panel shows all accessible variables at the breakpoint.
Watch expressions let you monitor custom values as you step through code.
Step Over, Step Into and Step Out let you navigate the execution flow.
lessons.challenge: Debug a recursive function by stepping through the call stack and observing variable changes at each level.
